Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:

Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The snapshot looks like December 2013, based on these figures:

- **Unemployment:** 7.0% matches the November 2013 rate, which was published in early December.
- **10-year yield:** 2.99% is about where it ended 2013.
- **Gold:** a 12-month drop of 28% fits 2013.
- **US equities:** a 12-month return of 32% matches the S&P 500 in 2013.

The 1-month equity return of +2.6% fits December 2013, which returned about 2.5%. In November the 1-month return was about 3%, but the 10-year yield was then about 2.75%, and the unemployment rate shown (7.0%) was published only in December. The 3-month change in unemployment of -0.3 also fits, since it was 7.3% in September.

I settle on December 2013.
